verdict.scope: AT THE SHIPPED GEOMETRY ONLY (window=12, limit=2, bucket_cap=1, reader chunk cap applied), ON BOTH POOL SHAPES: CHUNK-FREE pools (no raw session-transcript hits, so the reader's per-session cap is inert and the fused index space equals the reader's) and CHUNK-BEARING pools (raw transcript chunks, the shape the multi-session corpus is ingested as). The two do NOT agree, and neither number is universal — read the field's own shape. The sweep below reaches the graded top 5 at windows 3-6 ON A CHUNK-FREE POOL (the pick's ceiling is itself inside the top 5 there) — a different geometry, NOT the harness's tr_top_k, so it is not a way to reach the unit. A CHUNK-BEARING pool is graded at those same windows for that same ceiling reason, and stays graded at EVERY swept window from 3 through 13 because from window 7 on the reader's chunk cap has removed the raw chunks above the pick. Where a row carries `displacement_expressible: false` the capped pool is no deeper than the window (it holds the WHOLE pool, and six non-expressible rows are exactly the window's height), so its `additive` / `evicted_ids` / `deleted_sessions` are arithmetic, not measurement — read them only where it is true.
verdict.why: TWO INDEX SPACES, and only one of them is graded. The splice puts a tail pick at ceiling = window - budget in the caller's PRE-cap fused order (ranks 10-11 at window=12). But the harness fuses and THEN dedups — retrieve.py reassigns `annotated` to the fused order and the next statement is `pool = _dedup_pool(annotated, max_chunks_per_session=3)`, with `hits` = that pool — and recall_all@5 grades hits[:5] of the DEDUPED pool. dedup_pool caps RAW session-transcript chunks per session in rank order and never caps points/turn points, so the cap is a no-op on a chunk-free pool (fused rank == reader rank: 0 of 2 picks graded) and REMOVES SLOTS ABOVE the pick on a chunk-bearing one, lifting both picks to reader ranks 3-4 where recall_all@5 grades BOTH. The chunk-bearing pool also loses no session at the shipped window (net 0, deleted_sessions [], additive True), where the chunk-free one trades sB and sC away (net 0, deleted_sessions ['sB','sC'], additive False). So the unit is reachable-without-displacement ONLY on the geometry the arm targets, and NOT on a chunk-free pool — the opposite of what the pre-fix receipt stated as a universal. Placement='head' is a different answer on each shape, and it is MEASURED on each (the shipped-geometry chunk-bearing table publishes the head row beside the tail one): on a CHUNK-FREE pool head reaches ranks 0-1 by EVICTING sB and sC — both sole representatives — so it buys the unit with a swap, and that is exactly the #8713 (a) risk below. On a CHUNK-BEARING pool head also reaches ranks 0-1 but evicts NOTHING (`evicted_ids: []`, `deleted_sessions: []`) on all three pools INCLUDING `chunk_bearing_deep_window`, whose capped pool still fills the window so the emptiness is measured rather than entailed — because the chunk cap had already brought both picks inside the reader window at ranks 3-4, so the promotion is a pure RE-ORDER there. That is not a recommendation for head: on that shape the TAIL already reaches the graded top 5, so head buys no unit the default does not. ⚠️ What is NOT claimed here: this counterfactual has never been measured on the shipped corpus, and this instrument still has no judge and no dataset. The nearest measured analogue is #8713's C4 source-session RE-INJECTION arm — a DIFFERENT mechanism, and legible only when its capsweep receipt (docs/scoping/receipts/2026-09-17-2513-reinjection-capsweep-412470cd3.json) is split three ways: (a) the INJECTION's own eviction costs reader_surface@5 0.9436 -> 0.9289 — and the guard-ablated `inj_only` arm reads the same 0.9289, so the guard accounts for NONE of it; that is pure slot displacement damaging the reader surface, which is exactly the risk head placement carries; (b) the shared session-diverse guard — a session capped at 2 INSIDE the window — adds evidence_recall@5 0.527 -> 0.4706 (-5.6 pt, +4/-11 questions); (c) the closure is the guard's alone — `inj_only` is identical to `off` on every RECALL metric (recall_all@5 0.6761, session_recall@5 0.831, evidence_recall@5 0.527), its only difference being the two reader_surface@5 regressions the injection itself causes, per (a) — so the SAME arm NET GAINS recall_all@5 0.6761 -> 0.8592 (+0.1831, +13/-0). So the session-diverse re-order buys the ALL-sessions metric with item-level evidence, while unguarded displacement damages the reader surface for nothing. The only direct reading of head placement is temporal_leg.py's TF-IDF replay (-placement head -limit 2: recall@12 0.9506 vs 0.9228 tail), on a near-ceiling base that cannot represent the shipped 0/52 failure — which is why the placement A/B belongs on the eval lane and why this instrument reports it rather than ranking it.

what_this_is: the window arm's RETENTION baseline on the shipped wiring — hermetic, no reader/judge/graph/dataset/spend. It measures the ARM'S GEOMETRY, never answer quality.
what_this_is_not: NOT the #9097 Q3 exit measurement, and NOT a placement verdict. recall_all@5 on the frozen write_path corpus is owed to the eval lane, postponed by the owner ruling of 2026-11-02 (no eval runs while the P0/P1 queue is open).
